notes.decision: Translated 'the Seventh.' ⲥⲁϣϩ is dialectal/scribal variant of ⲥⲁϣϥ 'seven'; ⲙⲁⲍ- is the ordinal prefix (= Sah. ⲙⲉϩ-). The flanking ⲍ̄ (numeral 7) confirms.

Translated 'were called forth' (passive of ⲧⲱϩⲙ̄ 'summon, call, invite, seal'). The serial-emanation formula 'one from another' shows that ⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ here functions as the technical verb of cosmogonic emanation — each Father summoned/produced from the preceding one. Reused at line 26 (ⲁϩⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ 'he emanated').

Translated 'the Great Spirit.' Construction ⲡⲧⲛⲁⲟ + noun functions as 'the Great X' (cf. line 30 ⲡⲧⲛⲁⲟ ⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲣⲓⲧ 'the Great Beloved'). This is the Mother of Life in Western Manichaean cosmology, the first emanation of the Father of Greatness.

Feminine forms (ⲧϣⲁⲣⲡ, ⲧⲉⲧⲁⲥⲉⲓ, ⲁⲥⲟⲩⲱⲛⲍ̄) confirm that 'the Great Spirit' is grammatically feminine here, supporting the identification with the Mother of Life. Translated with feminine pronouns to preserve this.
Translated 'has been revealed.' ⲟⲩⲱⲗⲡ̄ here = ⲟⲩⲱⲛϩ ⲉⲃⲟⲗ 'manifest, reveal'; the perfect ⲁϩ- prefix gives stative-perfect sense.

ⲡⲟⲣⲟ taken as Lycopolitan writing of ⲡⲣ̄ⲣⲟ ('the king/kingship'); ϯ-ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ rendered 'gave kingship' / 'established kingship.' The verb is repeated with two complements: themselves (ⲛⲉⲩ ⲟⲩⲁⲉⲧⲟⲩ) and the aeons (ⲛ̄ⲛⲟⲩⲁⲓⲱⲛ).

Greek loanword προτομή = 'foremost cut, bust, image of the front part.' Retained as transliteration 'Protomē' rather than flattened to 'image' — the term carries the technical sense of the foremost emanation/forepart of the King of Lights, distinct from ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ ('likeness') and ⲙⲟⲣⲫⲏ ('form').

ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛϩⲏⲧ literally = 'expansion of heart.' Rendered 'pride-of-heart' to preserve the compound while signaling negative valence (Darkness's arrogance is destroyed). Same compound recurs in segment 16 of the Virgin of Light (positive context) — translated identically for consistency, even though the valence shifts; the Coptic uses one term.

ⲃⲓ-ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ̈-ϩⲁ literally 'lift-up-under' — preserves vertical/burden-bearing semantics: he carries upward what is beneath. The Pillar of Glory's defining function is the upward conveyance of the light-particles.

Verb of uncertain root; taken as a bearing/supporting verb cognate with ⲛⲟⲩϥ/ⲛⲏⲩ. Rendered 'bears up' to parallel the burden-bearer (Omophoros) image and the previous line's ⲃⲓ ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ̈. The Pillar = the great Omophoros who bears up all subordinate omophoroi.
Habitual relative: 'the one through whom they customarily give the eternal life.' Jesus the Radiance is the mediator of eternal life — passive 'is given' through him.

ⲧⲃⲓ ⲡϩⲏⲧ — 'to take/seize the heart' = to ravish, to enchant. The Virgin of Light's cosmic function is to seduce the Archons by displaying her image, making them release the captive light. 'Steals away the heart' preserves the active sense.

ⲕⲱ ⲁϩⲣⲛ̄ = 'set/place before (the face of).' ⲡⲉⲛⲉⲓⲛⲉ ('our likeness') taken as 'before our face/presence.' Jesus has placed the Mind of Light (and the apostles he fathers) in the holy Church, set before the community's likeness — i.e., where we may behold him.

Feminine 'great-one' modifying a lost feminine noun — likely ⲡⲁⲣⲑⲉⲛⲟⲥ ('maiden') by parallel with the Virgin of Light formula at L15. Note that the subject (Youth, ⲗⲓⲗⲟⲩ) is masculine but the modifier is feminine — indicating that the Youth is paired/identified with a feminine luminous figure. Left as lacuna without speculative restoration.
ⲉⲓ̈ⲥⲉⲭⲉ tentatively rendered 'gazing toward' (per accumulated vocabulary, possibly from Greek προσέχω). Two faces of the Youth direct their attention upward to the heaven he established.
'The Calling and the Hearing' — standard Manichaean technical pair (Mid. Pers. xrōštag ud padwāxtag), the two divine cries by which the soul is awakened. Capitalized as cosmic principles.

notes.coptic_form: ⲡⲉⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉⲩ ... ϩⲁⲧⲙ ⲡⲁⲓ̈ⲱⲧ ... ⲡⲉⲧⲁⲧⲉⲧⲛ̄ⲛⲉⲩ ... ϩⲁⲧⲙ̄ ⲡⲉⲧⲛⲓ̈ⲱⲧ
notes.decision: Direct echo of John 8:38 — Jesus's saying 'what I have seen with my Father I speak; and what you have seen with your father, you do.' The Manichaean text appropriates this as the Youth's word from the King's presence. Restoration of the bridging speech-formula in line 33 follows the editorial reconstruction.

Translated 'the fourth Father.' ⲙⲁⲍ-ϩⲧⲁⲩ = ordinal 'fourth' (cf. accumulated vocab ⲡϩⲧⲁⲩ 'the four'). The previous page presumably enumerated Fathers 1–3; this page begins with the fourth and reaches the fifth at line 12. The 'second' (line 6) and 'third' (line 9) inside this section refer to the three subsidiary ⲛⲟⲁⲙ 'powers' called by the fourth Father.

Translated 'powers' rather than 'mights/strengths' (per accumulated vocab note). In this enumeration the three ⲛⲟⲁⲙ are clearly distinct cosmological agents (Apostle, Call, Form of Light) parallel to the standard Manichaean triad of emanations, where 'powers' is the conventional rendering for δυνάμεις.

Translated 'at the time to bear.' ⲡⲥⲁⲡ = 'the turn / the season / the appointed time.' ϩⲣ̄ⲫⲟⲣⲉ = ⲣ̄- + Greek φορέω 'to bear/wear,' here used of the Apostle's incarnational bearing of the church-of-flesh.

Translated 'the Call' (capitalized). The technical Manichaean cosmological figure (Syriac qrīā, Greek κλῆσις) — the Call from the Father of Greatness which descends with the Apostle as his Twin/yokefellow. The following line's ⲛ̄ϣⲃⲣ̄ⲁⲟⲩⲏⲧ 'yokefellow' confirms this identification.

Translated 'yokefellow.' Compound ϣⲃⲏⲣ ('companion') + ⲟⲩⲏⲧ ('single, sole, joined'). Captures the unique-companion / united-partner sense — the Manichaean Twin/Syzygos who is bound to the apostle as one. 'Yokefellow' preserves the unitive bond.

Translated 'to attend him.' Verbal root ⲗⲁⲍⲧ̄ uncertain; possibly ⲗⲁϩⲥ̄ 'cleave/cling' or related to ⲗⲁϩⲙⲉϥ 'attendance.' Context (the Companion remaining beside the apostle in every place) supports a 'be near / attend / cling-to' sense.

Translated 'afflictions.' Greek loanword most likely θλίψις 'tribulation, affliction,' with Coptic spelling ⲑⲁⲓⲧⲓⲥ where -ⲗ- has been elided/assimilated. Paired here with κίνδυνοι 'dangers,' a standard Pauline-style doublet (Rom 8:35).

Translated 'the fifth Father also.' ⲙⲁⲍⲧⲟⲩ = ⲙⲁϩϯⲟⲩ 'fifth.' ⲍⲱϣ = ⲍⲱⲱϥ 'himself / also' (Lyc.). This Father differs from the fourth: where the fourth's Form of Light is received at renunciation (entry into the elect), the fifth's Form of Light is revealed at death (exit from the body).

Translated 'the one to hold.' ⲡⲟⲩⲉ = 'the one (of them),' introducing the first of the three angels. The series continues 'the second' (line 16) and 'the third' (line 17), each holding a different regalia.
Translated 'the prize.' Greek βραβεῖον — the victor's prize/award (Phil 3:14, 1 Cor 9:24). Standard Manichaean term for the eschatological reward presented to the soul at death.
Translated 'the diadem.' Likely the Coptic equivalent of διάδημα or a head-band/fillet, listed alongside ⲡⲥⲧⲉⲫⲁⲛⲟⲥ ('wreath') and ⲡⲕⲗⲁⲙ ('crown') as three distinct items of regalia.

Translated 'These are those of him who will recognize them.' Reading ⲡⲉⲧⲛⲁⲥⲛⲟⲩⲱⲛⲟⲩ as a form of ⲡⲉⲧⲛⲁⲥⲟⲩⲱⲛⲟⲩ 'who will know/recognize them' (with anomalous ⲥⲛ for ⲥⲟ). The cluster ⲛⲉⲓⲉⲧϩ̄ is morphologically obscure; tentatively parsed as ⲛⲉⲓ ⲉⲧ-ⲏ̄ⲡ '(those) who pertain to.'
Translated 'so that some (attain) life forever.' ⲭⲉ = 'so that, because.' ϣⲁ ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ = ϣⲁ ⲉⲛⲉϩ 'forever, eternally.' The construction 'some of life forever' is elliptical; supplying 'attain' for sense.
Translated 'men of mercy.' ⲥⲁⲛ- (collective 'men of') + ⲣ̄- + ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁϩⲣⲉ ('mercy, compassion'). Paired with 'the righteous of peace' as the two classes of recipients of the garments of light.
